description:
SURFACED by the fz-3sb adversarial audit (at 49126e966). fz-3sb correctly threads the real code_id into decode_token/decode_tokens so a token blob is decoded with ctx.code_id. But encode_tokens (token_payload.rs:9) bakes literal Vec<Token> payloads with REAL byte offsets ONLY during the initial parse of a submitted code's own text (called only from frontdoor.rs). derive_function_surface (jobs/source.rs:224) decodes an expanded function's token blob with expanded_source.code == FunctionSource.code (identity.rs:274) == the FUNCTION'S OWN defining code — which FunctionSourceExpander::expand (jobs/source.rs:401-430) never reassigns to the MACRO'S defining code (source.clone() swaps .source, not .code).

RISK: if a macro's quote-do-end body literally contains a type ascription / @spec / extern signature, and that quoted subtree is spliced verbatim into a caller defined in a DIFFERENT file (cross-module macro invocation IS supported — required_remote_macros / world.rs:943 run_macro_on_source), the baked token offsets belong to the MACRO's file but decode now uses the CALLER's code_id => Span = SourceId(caller) + offsets(macro file): an internally inconsistent span pointing at the wrong text.

STATUS: NOT confirmed reachable — needs nested quote-literal type syntax spliced through expansion WITHOUT re-parsing; the auditor did not trace to ground truth. NOT a regression from fz-3sb: the same scenario was already wrong before (SourceId(0) + offsets(macro file)); fz-3sb does not make a previously-correct case wrong.

TASK: (1) determine whether macro-spliced type/spec/extern tokens are a REAL reachable path (cross-file macro whose quote body has a malformed @type / type-ascription; observe the diagnostic span). (2) If reachable, thread the token's ORIGINATING code_id through expansion (carry it on the spliced subtree) rather than assuming the caller's. If NOT reachable, close won't-do with the evidence. VERIFY: a cross-file macro-spliced malformed type annotation points its diagnostic at the MACRO's file+offsets consistently. Related: fz-3sb, fz-ose.

comments.text:
VERDICT: NOT-REACHABLE (recommend close won't-do). Investigated at HEAD post-fz-3sb via concrete two-file production-path constructions.

MECHANISM IS REAL (confirmed): run_macro_on_source (world.rs:964-975) runs the macro's pre-compiled program on the CALLER's QuotedSourceRoot (owner) and wraps the result via source.subroot -- so a type-token blob baked literally in the macro's quote body (with the MACRO file's byte offsets, encoded at the macro file's index_code) is rematerialized into the CALLER's heap with those offsets copied verbatim, then derive_function_surface decodes it with expanded_source.code == the CALLER's code_id (jobs/source.rs:224-227). Cross-code macro expansion DOES occur: verified an 'import M, only: [tag: 1]' (or 'alias M' + 'require M') in file B expands a macro defined in file A (require-alone is insufficient: qualified M.tag hits 'macro/not-required'; the name must be bound via alias/import -- lookup_module_path has no global fallback). So a decoded Expr::Ascribe from a cross-code-spliced 'unquote(x) :: T' literally carries span{code_id: fileB, offsets: fileA} today.

WHY IT IS NOT OBSERVABLE (not reachable as a defect):
1. The ONLY type-blob-carrying construct reachable inside a 'quote do..end' body is the EXPRESSION-position '::' ascription. emit_type_payloads stays true inside quote bodies (only suppressed in bitstring literals, frontdoor.rs:1017-1018), so frontdoor.rs:689/695 DOES bake a '::' RHS type blob there.
2. All the OTHER type-blob producers -- @spec, @type, extern (frontdoor.rs:176-471), and named-fn typed params -- are item-level (parse_item), never reachable inside a quote body (quote -> parse_block_until -> parse_expr, no item dispatch). 'fn helper(a :: T), do:' inside quote is the lambda form (parse_lambda_expr, no '::'), does not parse ('expected ->').
3. Expression '::' ascription types are NEVER resolved or enforced: record_function_type_refs (source_publish.rs:349-372) collects refs ONLY from @spec, extern contracts, and clause param_annotations -- NOT from body Expr::Ascribe. Empirically 'unquote(x) :: %%%', ':: NoSuchType.t()', and ':: binary' (on an int) ALL drive to Resolved with NO diagnostic, cross-file AND single-file. So the mismatched span on the decoded node is never surfaced to any diagnostic (nor to inference).

Thus no .fz program under today's grammar+pipeline can produce a user-visible diagnostic (or any consumer) carrying the mismatched span. fz-3sb does not make any previously-correct case wrong.

SHARPER HAZARD CHARACTERIZATION (vs the ticket's assumption): the wrong-file span is NOT merely a future-grammar risk -- the inconsistent span{fileB, fileA-offsets} is ALREADY PRESENT on decoded Expr::Ascribe nodes from cross-code macro expansion. It is latent ONLY because body-expression ascription types are currently un-resolved/un-enforced/un-surfaced. The moment expression '::' ascriptions become type-checked or their span is ever surfaced (a natural evolution), the mismatch becomes observable with ZERO other changes. Recommend a forward-looking hardening ticket (either store SourceId inside the encoded token tuple in token_payload::encode_token so decode needs no external code_id, or carry the blob's originating code_id through expansion) rather than an active-bug fix.

No code change committed. No regression test added: expression ascriptions surface no diagnostic, so there is no correct-behavior span to lock in without first making the (deferred) fix. lib green 1238/0/6, working tree clean.

CLOSING WON'T-DO — NOT REACHABLE as an active defect (investigation at 6efa9fc16, no code change). The mechanism is REAL: run_macro_on_source (world.rs:964-975) rematerializes a macro file's baked type-token blob (macro-file offsets) into the caller's heap, and derive_function_surface (jobs/source.rs:224-227) decodes it with the caller's code_id => an inconsistent span{code_id: caller, offsets: macro-file} DOES land on decoded Expr::Ascribe nodes from a cross-file :: ascription. BUT it is not observable: the only type-blob construct reachable inside a quote body is the expression-position :: ascription (all of @spec/@type/extern/typed-params are item-level, unreachable inside quote), and expression :: ascription types are NEVER resolved/enforced/surfaced — record_function_type_refs (source_publish.rs:349-372) collects refs only from @spec/extern/clause param_annotations, not body Expr::Ascribe. Empirically 'unquote(x) :: %%%', ':: NoSuchType.t()', ':: binary' on an int all drive to Resolved with NO diagnostic, cross-file and single-file. So no .fz program under today's grammar+pipeline surfaces the mismatched span; fz-3sb made no previously-correct case wrong. The latent risk (the bad span already exists on the decoded node, waiting for ascription type-checking to make it observable) is CAPTURED, not dropped, by the correct-by-construction hardening ticket fz-h29 (self-describing token spans, which also obsoletes fz-3sb's code_id threading). Also filed the macro require/alias asymmetry noticed during repro: fz-osx.

title: Cross-code macro-spliced type/spec token blobs may stamp inconsistent spans (SourceId of caller + byte offsets of macro's file)
